name: Jurisdiction Expansion
description: Add a new national jurisdiction: real sourced rules, source registry regeneration, scope container registration, and canonical graph wiring.

steps.description: Research real, official sources for the new jurisdiction's rules (government and regulator publications). Consumes the request. Hands on candidate sources with what each says; fabricating a source is a failure. (Check the existing SOURCE_REGISTRY.md scope first when the walk shows it - methodology 34 heuristic.)
steps.name: research_sources

steps.description: Hand-curate real rules from the researched sources as JSON: condition, action, source (a citation each). No fabricated citations; a rule without a real source is left out. Hands on rules_json.
steps.name: curate_rules

steps.description: Specify the scope file to place under jurisdiction/national/ from the curated rules; boot dedup reuses an existing scope container for the same scope. Hands on the scope file content and path. Writing the file needs a file-write capability that is not registered.
steps.name: register_scope

steps.description: State what regenerating SOURCE_REGISTRY.md and SOURCE_REGISTRY.json from the real content requires (running tools/generate_jurisdiction_registry.py) and what the regenerated registry must show for the new scope. Running the script needs a script-execution capability that is not registered.
steps.name: regenerate_registry

steps.description: Specify the wiring of the new scope to the Global/EU baselines by min-id canonical (boot wiring or a manual canonical pass) and what edges must exist afterwards. Hands on the edge list expected.
steps.name: wire_graph

missing_capabilities: file write: create or overwrite files in the workspace (legacy CreateFile)
jurisdiction scope wiring pass (canonical min-id link of a new scope to the Global/EU baselines)
run a repository script (tools/generate_jurisdiction_registry.py) and read its output
